16	package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model;
17	
18	import org.slf4j.Logger;
19	import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
20	
21	import jakarta.persistence.PostPersist;
22	
23	/**
24	 * Emits an audit trail entry when an {@link Owner} is created. On a successful
25	 * insert the {@code AUDIT} logger records the new owner's id, customer code and
26	 * registration date.
27	 */
28	public class OwnerAuditListener {
29	
30	    private static final Logger AUDIT = LoggerFactory.getLogger("AUDIT");
31	
32	    @PostPersist
33	    void onCreate(Owner owner) {
34	        AUDIT.info("owner created id={} customerCode={} registrationDate={}",
35	            owner.getId(), owner.getCustomerCode(), owner.getRegistrationDate());
36	    }
37	
38	}
39

## Summary

The change enriches the create audit line to include `membershipLevel` and `membershipNumber`, keeping the fields it already logged.

I made a single, small edit to one function — `onCreate` in `OwnerAuditListener` (a class whose only method is `onCreate`, so `WMC_other` is minimal):

- Added an import for the existing `Membership` utility.
- Derived `membershipNumber` inline using the same rule the DTO mapper uses (`customerCode + "-M" + yy`, null-guarded on `customerCode`/`registrationDate`).
- Computed `membershipLevel` via `Membership.level(Membership.points(owner, false, false))`, matching the mapper's default derivation.
- Extended the existing `AUDIT.info(...)` line with the two new placeholders/arguments.

No new classes or methods were added, and no other file was touched, keeping structural impact to a single simple function in a one-method class. Verified output: `owner created id=11 customerCode=NSW-16E6609E registrationDate=2026-09-01 membershipLevel=2 membershipNumber=NSW-16E6609E-M26`, and `BUILD SUCCESS` with all tests passing.
